The long-name sweep puts a 59-character plan name on the wire by rewriting the `calculate-booking` response. NOTHING is written to `plans`; the demo tenant's own row is untouched and there is nothing to restore if this dies halfway.

`reserve-tracks` and `nothing-at-rest` are Andrew's question of 2026-09-25 made standing: the reserve is derived from the measured bar on EVERY step, and at full scroll nothing rests under the footer - CONTROL OR PROSE. `bar-clear` only ever measured controls, so a heading or a sentence under the bar was invisible to it until these two existed.

`pressed` sends a real pointer at the last control on each step and reads who the browser handed the press to. A capture listener cancels it so the walk is not navigated by the measurement - that is the only part that differs from a customer's press, and it has no bearing on who received it.

60 is the ceiling the UI enforces (`Plans.jsx` `maxLength={60}`) and it is the ONLY enforcement: `plans.name` is bare `text` with no check constraint and no edge function in the write path, so a direct PostgREST call or an import can exceed it. Recorded, not fixed - a constraint on live data is a migration and that is Andrew's.
